newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money edges up in busy pre-expiry trade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money edges up in busy pre-expiry trade.

text.p: Dutch call money crept somewhat higher to 2.25 percent in busy trade on Wednesday afternoon, after reaching a low of 1.88 percent earlier during the session.
Dealers said the volatility in overnight money, which fell as low as 1.50 percent bid on Tuesday from 3.06 last Friday, attracted more activity.
"In a stable market, it's not that exciting. But when price swings are as big as they are now, it's worthwhile to go shopping to see what others are offering," one dealer said.
On Friday, the current credit quota expires. It ran only one month instead of the usual three months.
"Market players have been careful because of the short credit quota," one dealer said.
Call money rates tend to be increasingly volatile towards the end of the credit quota expiry.
Dealers said they expected call rates to remain low until Friday's expiry, after which they saw them edging higher.

On Friday, the Dutch central bank will implement its modified monetary policy detailed yesterday, in a move to prepare for EMU, but dealers said the changes had been broadly known before the announcement and did not have any impact on today's trade.
"What was formally announced yesterday, has been informally known for quite some time already," one dealer said.
Dealers said Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) were set slightly higher than on Tuesday by the Finance Ministry's Agent.
DTCs maturing in June were set at 3.16 percent, those in July at 3.17 percent and those in December at 3.20 percent.
Deposits were quoted unchanged from Tuesday, with one month-deposits quoting at 3.12/20 percent bid/ask and three month-deposits at 3.16/24.
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark, trading at 112.434 guilders per 100 marks.
